## Saturation adjustment in the step (reactions in the thermo block) {#sec-ch10-satadj}

### Summary

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**What it does.** Brings every interior cell to phase equilibrium once per step, at fixed density and fixed
internal energy, by moving mass between each vapour and its condensates.
**Switch.** None of its own: on whenever the thermo block declares reactions; kintera's `uv-solver`, `max-iter`
and `ftol` tune the solve. **Requires.** The whole-column conserved limiter, which runs just before it.
**Runs.** On the last RK stage, interior cells only, before the boundary fill.
**Defining equation.** @eq-ch10-satadj-state.
:::

Phase change is fast compared with the dynamics, so snapy does not resolve it inside the RK stages. It lets the
stages advect vapour and condensate as tracers that carry their own reference energies, and once per step,
after the last stage has been averaged, it hands each interior cell to kintera's fixed-volume fixed-energy
equilibrium solve (@sec-ch02-saturation) and writes the new mass fractions back. Latent heat is never a separate
source: it is the difference of the species reference energies $u^{\star}_n$ (NOTATION.md section 2), so moving
mass between phases at fixed $\rho e$ changes the temperature and leaves $E$ alone. This section is the snapy
side of that solve: when it runs, what it is handed, what it writes, and what happens when it fails.

The adjustment is on whenever the thermo block of the YAML card lists reactions; there is no flag to turn it off
while keeping the reactions. Its failures do not stop the step: they are counted and turned into redo cause 16
(@sec-ch10-redo). The ghost cells are not adjusted; they are refilled from the adjusted interior afterwards
(the #206 ordering, [chengcli/snapy#206](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/issues/206)).

### Derivation

The derivation of the equilibrium itself, its energy constraint and its active-set solve, is
@sec-ch02-saturation; it is not repeated here. What this section adds is the state handed to it and the proof that
the write-back changes only the species rows.

Step (6) of the stage update forms, in every interior cell, the total density, the internal energy density and
the mass fractions from the conserved state:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\rho &= \rho_{\mathrm{d}} + \sum_{n}\rho_n,\\
\rho e &= E - \tfrac12\rho\lvert\mathbf v\rvert^2,\\
y_n &= \rho_n/\rho .
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch10-satadj-state}

@eq-ch10-satadj-state is formed as `rho`, `ie` and `yfrac` in `MeshBlockImpl::forward`
([`meshblock.cpp:800-806`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/mesh/meshblock.cpp#L800-L806), `yfrac`).
kintera's `ThermoYImpl::forward` receives $\rho$ and $\rho e$ by value and $y_n$ by reference, solves the
equilibrium at fixed $\rho$ and fixed $\rho e$, and overwrites $y_n$
([`kintera thermo_y.cpp:275-383`](https://github.com/chengcli/kintera/blob/c55b13b2204997d2d09e04498558ab9495d8ee77/src/thermo/thermo_y.cpp#L275-L383)).
snapy then writes $\rho_n \leftarrow \rho\,y_n$ for every species row, with the same $\rho$ it handed in
([`meshblock.cpp:816`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/mesh/meshblock.cpp#L816), `yfrac`).

Three consequences follow from these lines alone. First, the energy row is not written, so $E$ is unchanged to the
last bit; since momentum is not written either, $\rho e = E - \tfrac12\rho\lvert\mathbf v\rvert^2$ is unchanged as
long as $\rho$ is. Second, the dry row is not written, so $\rho_{\mathrm{d}}$ is unchanged. Third, $\rho$ is
unchanged if and only if $\sum_n y_n$ is: the phase reactions move mass between species rows and never create it,
so kintera returns fractions whose sum equals the input sum up to its solver tolerance, and $\rho$ after the write-back
equals $\rho$ before to that tolerance. The energy is therefore conserved exactly and the total water to the
tolerance of the phase solve; `test_wall_saturation` measures both below $10^{-12}$ relative over a whole run
(Tests layer). No executable check is added in this chapter: the identities above are read off the code, and the
solve's own algebra is checked by `saturation_check.py` of chapter 2.

### Numerical method

@fig-ch10-satadj-timeline places the adjustment in the step. Every stage ends with the RK average and a
whole-column call of the conserved limiter
([`meshblock.cpp:755-756`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/mesh/meshblock.cpp#L755-L756), `apply_conserved_limiter_`).
On the last stage, and only if the thermo has reactions, the limiter runs once more and the adjustment follows
([`meshblock.cpp:796-798`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/mesh/meshblock.cpp#L796-L798), `reactions`),
so kintera never sees a negative species density. The solve is restricted to interior cells through the
`exterior(false)` part of the block
([`meshblock.cpp:811-814`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/mesh/meshblock.cpp#L811-L814), `exterior`),
and the physical ghosts are refilled from the adjusted interior by `apply_boundaries`, after the gravity-work fixer
([`meshblock.cpp:841`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/mesh/meshblock.cpp#L841)).
The order of that fill relative to the exchange and the corner refresh is @sec-ch11-timing.
Every quantity here is a cell average; the adjustment is pointwise in each cell, with no stencil.

The call passes `warm_start = true`: kintera reuses the active set of its last call when the shape and the
device match, and starts cold otherwise
([`kintera thermo_y.cpp:293-310`](https://github.com/chengcli/kintera/blob/c55b13b2204997d2d09e04498558ab9495d8ee77/src/thermo/thermo_y.cpp#L293-L310), `reuse`).
A cell the solve could not adjust is marked by a negative diagnostic and counted; on CPU kintera also warns at once,
on CUDA the count stays on the device until snapy reads it after the step (@sec-ch10-redo).

```{python}
#| label: fig-ch10-satadj-timeline
#| fig-cap: "Where the saturation adjustment sits in one RK step. Each box is one step of the stage update, read top to bottom; the last three boxes run on the last stage only, and the final box is the driver's call after the step. Green outlines mark operations, black arrows the order."
#| fig-alt: "Six boxes in a column: stage-0 save and counter drain; per-stage limiter; last-stage limiter; UV adjustment of interior cells; boundary fill; check_redo after the step."
#| echo: false
from snapy_report.ch10.fig_satadj_timeline import make_fig
make_fig()
```

3. The state of @eq-ch10-satadj-state ([`meshblock.cpp:800-806`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/mesh/meshblock.cpp#L800-L806), `yfrac`).
4. The module found by name, so that every EOS type with a ThermoY is served ([`meshblock.cpp:808-809`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/mesh/meshblock.cpp#L808-L809), `pthermo`).
5. The interior-only call with the warm start ([`meshblock.cpp:811-814`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/mesh/meshblock.cpp#L811-L814), `warm_start`).
6. The write-back of the species rows ([`meshblock.cpp:816`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/mesh/meshblock.cpp#L816), `yfrac`).
7. The boundary fill ([`meshblock.cpp:841`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/mesh/meshblock.cpp#L841), `apply_boundaries`).

The step has no setup check of its own and prints no warning; kintera's CPU warning on a failed cell is the only
message a user sees, and the redo log line of @sec-ch10-redo names the cause.

### Tests

| test (ctest name) | what it asserts | tolerance | where the tolerance comes from |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test_wall_saturation.release` | energy and water over a run | $10^{-12}$ rel. | test threshold |
| `test_balance_column.release` | moist column stays at rest | $10^{-10}$ | dry case's bound |
| `test_vic_moist_device_python` | CPU equals CUDA, one step | $10^{-9}$ | 17 times the recorded gap |
| `test_check_redo_saturation_python` | a failed cell redoes the step | logical | failure protocol |

: Tests of the saturation adjustment in the step. Assertions are read from the test sources at the pin; none was
run for this draft. {#tbl-ch10-satadj-tests}

`test_wall_saturation` runs a 64 m column next to a lower and an upper wall, once condensing and once evaporating,
and asserts relative drifts of total energy and total water below $10^{-12}$ and an actual phase change
([`test_wall_saturation.cpp:63-89`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/tests/test_wall_saturation.cpp#L63-L89), `EXPECT_LT`).
The moist `test_balance_column` case holds a subsaturated column, so it shows the adjustment leaves a balanced
state at rest, with the condensate row exactly zero and the vapour within $10^{-12}$
([`test_balance_column.cpp:505-513`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/tests/test_balance_column.cpp#L505-L513), `f_balanced`).
`test_vic_moist_device_python` compares CPU and CUDA for one moist step; its bound $10^{-9}$ is about 17 times the
gap recorded in its source comment
([`test_vic_moist_device.py:19-20`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/tests/test_vic_moist_device.py#L19-L20), `DEVICE_TOL`);
that comment's number has no sha, deck or run of its own and is not quoted as evidence here. Coverage: the wall test
is registered on CPU and, in CUDA builds, on CUDA; the device test exists only in CUDA builds; no test runs the
adjustment on more than one rank. Measured numbers at the pin are **missing evidence** until a pinned build runs
these entries (@sec-ch15-ch10-tests).

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
Only interior cells are adjusted; ghosts are copies, so a scheme that reads ghost species before the next boundary
fill sees unadjusted values. A failed cell is left unadjusted for the rest of the step and costs a redo.
:::

- No decomposed moist test with reflecting walls exists ([chengcli/snapy#208](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/issues/208)).
- The warm start is discarded whenever kintera is called with another shape or device in between, for example
  by a diagnostic call from Python; correctness is unaffected, cost is not measured.
- Water is conserved to the phase solve's tolerance, not to round-off; the solve's tolerances are those of
  @sec-ch02-saturation.
- The switch coverage matrix (@sec-ch12-matrix) has no row for moist runs; the combinations with
  `SNAP_WB_REF4`, `SNAP_X1_CENTROID_EXACT` and the face gravity work are covered only by the moist
  `test_balance_column` arms.
